name: Definition (ḥadd)
definition: A definition of a term of grammar that takes in everything it names and keeps out everything else (jāmiʿ māniʿ), in the way of the logicians.
body: Handbooks open their chapters with a ḥadd, and the commentaries test it word by word: each word is a 'genus' (jins) or a 'difference' (faṣl) that excludes something, and the commentator asks what it keeps out. Al-Ājurrūmiyya's first line is the classic case: 'speech is the utterance, composed, useful, by convention', and its commentators explain why each of the four words is there. Al-Rummānī's Kitāb al-Ḥudūd collects the definitions of grammar.

examples.arabic: الكَلَامُ هُوَ اللَّفْظُ المُرَكَّبُ المُفِيدُ بِالوَضْعِ
examples.text: Al-Ājurrūmiyya's definition of speech: utterance, composed, useful, by convention; each word keeps something out.
